comments.why_zh: 一场精彩的采访，强调了成功中的运气和谦逊态度。
comments.quote_zh: 在那场非常精彩的Numberphile采访中，他特别强调了成功中的运气因素。
comments.text_zh: 虽然我不是那种会追捧亿万富翁的人，但我发现他的人生故事和个性真的很吸引人。他似乎确实保持着谦逊的态度，而在那场非常精彩的Numberphile采访中，他特别强调了成功中的运气因素。他以非常有针对性的方式捐了大量资金，而这些捐赠极其成功。我想，正是因为他的谦逊态度、不爱自我宣传等等，他在某些圈子之外有点不为人知，但他在某些领域的影响很大。虽然我希望我们的国家不必依赖亿万富翁来牵头推动各种倡议——这往往走错方向——但Simons绝对是好榜样之一。[VIDEO]
comments.text: While I'm not one to fawn after billionaires, I found his life story and personality really fascinating. He really seemed to maintain a humble approach, and in the Numberphile interview, which is excellent, he really emphasized the notion of luck in success. He donated a ton of money in very targeted ways that have been extremely successful. I think because of his humble approach, lack of self-promotion, etc., he's a bit unknown outside certain circles, but his impact in certain areas has been big. While I wish that our country didn't have to rely on billionaires spearheading initiatives, which often goes the wrong way, Simons was absolutely an example of one of the good ones. [VIDEO]

comments.story_title: Medallion Fund “Stretches Explanation to the Limit,” Professor Claims
comments.why_zh: Simons 说他们主要用 ML 和简单技术，再加上市场冲击相关的数学。
comments.quote_zh: 值得看看 Numberphile 对 Simons 的采访
comments.text_zh: > Medallion 基金自 1993 年起就对外部资本关闭，而对这只旗舰基金年度回报的分析表明，每年都会进行大规模的分配，以让基金规模大致保持不变。例如，尽管 Medallion 在 2010 到 2018 年间每年报告的净回报都高于 29%，但该基金的管理资产规模在这整个期间一直保持在约 100 亿美元。这在我看来说明，无论他们在利用什么机会，一旦他们扩大基金规模（比如通过复利滚动回报），这些机会就会很快消失。值得看看 Numberphile 对 Simons 的采访（[VIDEO]）。他在那里表示，他们主要使用 ML 和其他相对简单的技术，只在预测一笔交易会如何影响市场时才会用上一些更高级的数学。这与他们必须让交易规模保持相对较小才能维持这种盈利水平的说法很吻合。
comments.text: > The Medallion fund has been closed to external capital since 1993, and analysis of the flagship fund’s annual returns suggests that significant distributions are made each year to keep the fund about the same size. For example, despite the fact that Medallion reported annual net returns above 29 percent every year between 2010 and 2018, the fund’s assets under management stayed at about $10 billion throughout that period. This suggests to me that whatever opportunities they're exploiting, they would vanish quickly if they would increase the fund's size (e.g. by compounding returns). It's worth taking a look at the Numberphile interview with Simons ( [VIDEO] ). There he suggests that they're mostly using ML and other relatively simple techniques, with a bit of more advanced math when it comes to predicting how a trade will move the market. This chimes in well with the idea that they have to keep their trades relatively small in order to remain this profitable.

comments.author: bmitc
comments.story_title: A Jim Simons Market Mystery – Solved? Not:-)
comments.quote_zh: 完整的Numberphile采访
comments.text_zh: 这是因为James Simons是个严肃且真正聪明、知识有深度的人，因此他不需要对随便什么事都发表意见。他还以非常隐秘的方式赚了很多钱。我不确定为什么有人会指望他详细阐述Renaissance Technologies是怎么做到的。Simons在一些非常严肃且先进的科学研究上投入的钱比一些政府还多。我猜他忙着处理自己的投资和慈善事业。Musk则忙着推销自己，填补他那填不满的自我。在Simons与Chris Anderson的那场TED采访中，你能看出他有时对Chris挺不耐烦，尤其是8:30左右Chris提到Simons的“非凡头脑”时。在我看来，Simons像是个相当务实、谦逊的人，并不特别享受奉承。Chris甚至在采访最后抛出了一句Musk的话，想引Simons说出类似的套话，但Simons巧妙地避开了这种空洞的引语。[LINK] 最有意思的是，你能看出Simons对科学和数学的喜爱；他在接近结尾提到自己对生命起源研究的投资时，也暗示了这种兴趣。我知道的Simons有两场有趣的演讲或采访：* 完整的Numberphile采访：[VIDEO] * 他在MIT所做的关于自己人生的演讲：[LINK] Simons实际上把自己很大一部分成功归因于运气。
comments.text: It's because James Simons is a serious and actually intelligent person with depth of knowledge, and thus, he is one that doesn't need to opine on random things. He also makes a lot of money in a very secretive way. I'm not sure why anyone expects him to expound in detail on how Renaissance Technologies does it. Simons also spends more money than some governments on very serious and advanced scientific research. I suppose he's rather busy with all his investments and philanthropy. Musk is busy selling himself and filling his unfillable ego. You can see in Simons' TED interview with Chris Anderson how he gets rather annoyed with Chris at times, particularly when Chris mentions Simons' "amazing mind" at around 8:30. Simons seems, to me, to be a rather pragmatic and humble person who doesn't particularly enjoy flattery. Chris even throws out a quote by Musk at the very end of the interview, fishing for some similar platitude from Simons, but Simons deftly avoids giving out such an empty quote. [LINK] Most interestingly, you can tell Simons' like of science and mathematics and alludes to his interest when he mentions his investment into the origins of life towards the end. There are two interesting talks or interviews I know of with Simons: * Full-length Numberphile interview: [VIDEO] * His lecture on his life given at MIT: [LINK] Simons actually attributes a lot of his success to luck.

comments.author: WestCoastJustin
comments.story_title: Ask HN: I am interested in reading about techniques HFT firms use
comments.why_zh: 对Renaissance一位创始人的精彩采访。
comments.quote_zh: 这是对其中一位创始人非常精彩的一场采访
comments.text_zh: 你可以翻翻这些公司大多数招聘启事，了解它们的组织架构和技术栈。我看的时候，除了较早的纪录片，几乎没什么公开信息。Nanex有一些挺不错的接线图，如果你去搜，还能找到几段视频片段。别太兴奋，你不会了解到什么超级秘密策略之类的东西。这本书不错[LINK]，它大致在高层次上解释了你会如何建立一家公司来研究这类东西（我记得是最后几章之一）。你需要极其深厚/专业的硬件/网络团队、数据采集（想想从抓包到数据）人员、清理和维护庞大数据仓库的人、内部工具团队、量化分析师、交易员、管理/行政人员等等。在这个层面上，仅仅把光纤接到各个交易所，可能就要花费数千万。当你去翻那些招聘启事时，你可以把这些岗位塞进你对这个流程的心智模型里，然后开始看出它可能是怎么搭建起来的。那本书不错，但如果你刚接触这个主题，它几乎读不下去。至少对我来说是这样。这些年来我不得不读了三到四遍，随着知识增长仍能发现新东西。我不知道rentec是不是高频交易公司，也不知道他们用什么策略，但这是对其中一位创始人非常精彩的一场采访[VIDEO]。
comments.text: You can troll through the job postings of most of these companies and learn about their org structures and tech stacks. When I looked almost nothing is public other than older documentaries. Nanex had some neat wiring diagrams and a few videos clips if you google them. Don't get too excited you're not going to learn about some super secret strategy or anything. This book was good [LINK] in that is sort of explains at a high level how you'd build a company to look at something like this (think it was one of the last chapters). You'll need extremely deep/skilled hardware/networking groups, data acquisitions (think packet capture to data) folks, people to clean and maintenance massive the data repos, internal tool teams, quantitative analysts, traders, management/admin, etc. At this level just getting the fiber to each exchange likely costs many many millions. When you go and look through those job postings you can sort of slot these into your mental model of this flow and start to see how it might be put together. That book is good but if you are new to the topic it will be almost unreadable. At least it was for me. I had to read it 3-4 times over the years and still find new things as my knowledge grows. I don't know if rentec is a HFT firm or what strategies they use but this was a really good interview with one of the founders [VIDEO] .
